text: From 2010 to 2020, we had the golden years of deterministic matching where it was very easy to run an ad and understand with precision who installed the app.
speaker: Austin Hay
context: Austin is opening the podcast by explaining the dramatic shift in mobile app attribution that has fundamentally changed marketing technology. IDFA (Identifier for Advertisers) was Apple's unique identifier that allowed precise tracking of users from ads to app installs. PII stands for Personally Identifiable Information. Austin explains how the elimination of deterministic matching (precise, definitive tracking) has created a paradox where ad networks are becoming more sophisticated while marketers have less visibility into their spending effectiveness.
text_ko: 2010년부터 2020년까지는 결정론적 매칭(deterministic matching)의 황금기였어요. 광고를 집행하면 누가 앱을 설치했는지 아주 정확히 파악하기가 정말 쉬웠어요.
text_zh: 2010到2020年这十年，可以说是确定性匹配(deterministic matching)的黄金时代，那时候投广告特别简单，能很精准地知道是谁安装了你的应用。
text_es: Del 2010 al 2020 fueron los años dorados de la atribución determinística, donde era súper fácil lanzar un anuncio y saber con exactitud quién se descargó la app.
key_sentence: we had the golden years of deterministic matching where it was very easy to run an ad and understand with precision who installed the app.
original_text: From 2010 to 2020, we had the golden years of deterministic matching where it was very easy to run an ad and understand with precision who installed the app. Maybe you didn't know their name, but you actually would know their IDFA and you could tie that to their PII. You can't do that anymore. So, what that means is these ad networks are becoming more complex, sophisticated, and interesting, right at the same time that it's harder for marketers to really understand how they're spending money.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by a predictable outcome based on specific inputs or conditions, leaving no room for randomness or uncertainty.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, deterministic models are often used in data analytics and advertising to ensure that outcomes can be reliably forecasted based on known variables.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'deterministic' implies certainty, it may not account for external factors that could influence outcomes, making it less applicable in highly variable environments.

vocabulary.definition: The quality of being exact, accurate, and clearly defined, often measured in terms of consistency and reliability.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of advertising and data analysis, precision is crucial for targeting the right audience and measuring the effectiveness of campaigns.
vocabulary.nuance: Precision implies a high degree of accuracy, but it may not always guarantee relevance or effectiveness in broader strategic contexts.

text: Marketing technology is like this very amorphous, cross-functional discipline that lives at the crossroads of product and growth and engineering and marketing. It brings together processes and systems from a wide range of disciplines.
speaker: Austin Hay
context: Lenny asks Austin to define what MarTech (Marketing Technology) is and what someone in MarTech does. Austin is explaining that MarTech is an interdisciplinary field that sits between multiple departments - product, growth, engineering, and marketing. He describes it as managing both third-party tools (external platforms like analytics or email tools) and first-party solutions (custom-built internal systems), similar to how a product manager approaches their role.
text_ko: 마케팅 테크놀로지(marketing technology, 마테크)는 제품(product), 그로스(growth), 엔지니어링(engineering), 마케팅(marketing)이 만나는 교차점에 자리한 꽤 모호하고 교차 기능적인(cross-functional) 분야예요. 다양한 분야의 프로세스와 시스템을 한데 모아서 연결해 줘요.
text_zh: 营销技术这个领域比较模糊，跨部门性质很强，处在产品、增长、工程和营销的交叉点上。它把各个不同领域的流程和系统都整合到一起了。
text_es: La tecnología de marketing es como una disciplina muy difusa y transversal que está en el cruce entre producto, crecimiento, ingeniería y marketing. Junta procesos y sistemas de un montón de áreas diferentes.
key_sentence: Marketing technology exists at the crossroads of product, growth, engineering, and marketing.
original_text: Marketing technology is like this very amorphous, cross-functional discipline that lives at the crossroads of product and growth and engineering and marketing. It brings together processes and systems from a wide range of disciplines. And I think really the way to think about marketing technology is it's a product manager whose specific role and focus is the system or the third party or first party platform.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to a team or process that involves members from multiple functional areas or departments within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, cross-functional teams are often formed to leverage diverse expertise and perspectives to solve complex problems or drive projects that require collaboration across various departments.
vocabulary.nuance: This term emphasizes collaboration and integration, and is often used in contexts where silos between departments are being broken down.

vocabulary.definition: A series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular end or outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, processes are critical for ensuring efficiency, consistency, and quality in operations, often documented and optimized for better performance.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'processes' can refer to any sequence of actions, in a business context it often implies a formalized and repeatable method.

vocabulary.definition: A set of interconnected components or elements that work together to achieve a common goal or function.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and technology, systems are used to integrate various processes and technologies, facilitating communication and data flow across an organization.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'systems' often implies a level of complexity and interdependence, and is typically used when discussing structured frameworks or models.

text: And everybody thinks that marketing technology is just the third party tools, but actually it's designing, architecting and building that stuff on top of your third party tools. That's how you actually have a lot of velocity is thinking about not just build versus buy.
speaker: Austin Hay
context: Austin is explaining the slice of work that a MarTech person would take from a growth team when companies reach the point of needing dedicated MarTech support. He's describing how MarTech involves both purchasing third-party tools and building custom solutions on top of them. The "build versus buy" decision framework traditionally meant choosing one or the other, but Austin advocates for "build and buy" - purchasing tools for the foundation and building custom features on top.
text_ko: 사람들은 마케팅 테크(marketing technology)를 서드파티 도구(third-party tools)로만 생각하는 경향이 있어요. 그런데 실제로는 그 서드파티 도구 위에서 무엇을 설계하고, 아키텍처를 만들고, 직접 구축하는 게 핵심이에요. 진짜로 속도(velocity)를 내려면 단순히 직접 만들까 사서 쓸까(build versus buy)만 고민하는 게 아니라 전체 구조와 조합을 생각해야 해요.
text_zh: 大家都以为营销技术(marketing technology)就是那些第三方工具，但其实真正的核心是在这些第三方工具基础上去设计、搭建和开发东西。要想真正提速，关键不只是考虑自己开发还是直接买现成的。
text_es: Y todo el mundo piensa que la tecnología de marketing son solo las herramientas de terceros, pero en realidad se trata de diseñar, estructurar y construir cosas encima de esas herramientas externas. Así es como realmente puedes tener mucha velocidad: no pensando solo en si desarrollar internamente o comprar algo ya hecho.
key_sentence: Velocity comes from building on top of third party tools, not just buying them.
original_text: And everybody thinks that marketing technology is just the third party tools, but actually it's designing, architecting and building that stuff on top of your third party tools. That's how you actually have a lot of velocity is thinking about not just build versus buy. It's build and buy now. So, you buy the tool to get 90% of the way there and then you build the cool thing on top with the other 10%.

vocabulary.definition: The process of designing and planning the structure and components of a system or project.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, architecting involves creating a blueprint for software, systems, or infrastructure that aligns with organizational goals and user needs.
vocabulary.nuance: While often used in technical contexts, architecting can also imply a strategic approach to problem-solving and innovation.

vocabulary.definition: The speed at which a project or process is completed, often measured in terms of output over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and technology, velocity refers to the rapid development and deployment of products or features, which is crucial for maintaining competitive advantage.
vocabulary.nuance: Velocity can carry a positive connotation of efficiency and agility, but excessive focus on speed may compromise quality.

vocabulary.definition: A strategic decision-making process that evaluates whether to create a solution in-house (build) or purchase an existing solution from an external provider (buy).
vocabulary.businessContext: This concept is critical in technology and business strategy, as it influences resource allocation, cost management, and time to market.
vocabulary.nuance: The choice between build versus buy often reflects a company's capabilities, priorities, and long-term vision, with each option carrying its own risks and benefits.

text: I think all marketing technologists at some level are ICs. I think it's a great job personally, because I get to be an IC and a manager.
speaker: Austin Hay
context: Lenny asks whether MarTech people do the work themselves or build teams with engineers. Austin explains that MarTech professionals are Individual Contributors (ICs) who must maintain hands-on technical expertise. Unlike traditional management roles where you might delegate technical work, MarTech requires you to be the senior technical expert on both internal systems (first party) and external tools (third party), which means staying involved in the actual implementation work.
text_ko: 저는 모든 마케팅 테크놀로지 전문가(marketing technologists)가 어느 정도는 개인 기여자(Individual Contributor)라고 생각해요. 개인적으로는 개인 기여자이자 매니저로 일할 수 있어서 이 직무가 정말 좋아요.
text_zh: 我觉得所有做营销技术的人，本质上都是个贡献者(IC)。我个人觉得这工作特别好，因为我既能做具体的事，又能带团队。
text_es: Creo que todos los tecnólogos de marketing son, en el fondo, colaboradores individuales. Para mí es un trabajo genial, porque puedo ser tanto colaborador individual como manager.
key_sentence: I think it's a great job personally, because I get to be an IC and a manager.
original_text: I think all marketing technologists at some level are ICs. I think it's a great job personally, because I get to be an IC and a manager. You have to be an IC in that, you are the most senior technical expert on all first party and third party systems. So, you have to know really well how third party tools work and you don't know that without doing the work yourself.

vocabulary.definition: Professionals who specialize in the application of technology to solve problems or create products, often possessing a deep understanding of technical systems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and product development, technologists play a crucial role in integrating technology with business strategies to enhance efficiency and innovation.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often connotes a blend of technical expertise and practical application, distinguishing these professionals from purely theoretical scientists.

vocabulary.definition: An individual responsible for overseeing and coordinating the work of others, ensuring that organizational goals are met efficiently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate settings, managers play a critical role in guiding teams, allocating resources, and making strategic decisions to drive performance.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can suggest a level of authority and responsibility, but may also imply a need for interpersonal skills and adaptability in leadership styles.

text: I almost view them like a true quarterback every [inaudible] says people are quarterbacks. But really marketing technology because it lives between so many departments, it plays that role of having to call plays and pull on different departments.
speaker: Austin Hay
context: Austin continues explaining the cross-functional nature of MarTech roles. He's describing how MarTech professionals need to coordinate across multiple departments - they might need to work with the head of revenue operations to change something in Salesforce, talk to the VP of product for platform changes, or rely on the data team for resources. The quarterback analogy emphasizes how they orchestrate plays across different functional areas rather than having direct authority over team members.
text_ko: 저는 사실 그걸 진짜 쿼터백(quarterback)처럼 보는 편이에요. 사람들이 다들 쿼터백이라고 말하긴 하는데, 마케팅 테크놀로지(marketing technology)는 여러 부서 사이에 걸쳐 있어서 전술을 지시하고 다양한 부서를 끌어모아 조율하는 역할을 해요.
text_zh: 我觉得他们就像真正的四分卫(quarterback)一样，虽然每个人都说自己是四分卫。但营销技术因为要跟这么多部门打交道，确实起到了那种统筹协调的作用，需要制定策略，还要调动各个部门的资源。
text_es: Yo casi los veo como un verdadero mariscal de campo (quarterback), porque todo el mundo dice que la gente son mariscales de campo. Pero realmente la tecnología de marketing, como está entre tantos departamentos, juega ese papel de tener que dirigir las jugadas y coordinar con diferentes áreas.
key_sentence: Marketing technology calls plays and pulls on different departments like a quarterback.

vocabulary.definition: Distinct divisions within an organization, each responsible for specific functions or areas of expertise.
vocabulary.businessContext: Departments such as marketing, finance, and human resources play critical roles in the overall operation and strategy of a business.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often conveys a sense of specialization, but it can also highlight potential barriers to communication and collaboration between units.

vocabulary.definition: The function or position that an individual or entity occupies within a specific context or organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, clearly defined roles help delineate responsibilities and expectations, facilitating effective teamwork and accountability.
vocabulary.nuance: While it denotes a specific function, 'role' can also imply a degree of flexibility, as individuals may take on multiple roles depending on the situation.

text: I tend to take a little bit of a different approach than most, which is like I think you should always be thinking about the future.
speaker: Austin Hay
context: Austin is explaining his philosophy for how growth managers should think about MarTech decisions beyond just immediate needs. He's addressing the balance between short-term execution and long-term planning. "Over index towards the future" means focusing too heavily on future needs at the expense of current priorities like achieving product-market fit. Austin advocates for making tool decisions that consider future scalability without sacrificing present objectives.
text_ko: 저는 대부분의 사람들과는 조금 다르게 접근하는 편이에요. 제 생각엔 항상 미래를 염두에 둬야 해요.
text_zh: 我的想法跟大多数人不太一样，我觉得应该时刻考虑未来的发展。
text_es: Yo suelo tener un enfoque un poco distinto al de la mayoría, y es que creo que siempre hay que estar pensando en el futuro.
key_sentence: I think you should always be thinking about the future.
original_text: I tend to take a little bit of a different approach than most, which is like I think you should always be thinking about the future. That doesn't necessarily mean you should make design choices that over index towards the future so much that you miss product market fit or you make poor product decisions. But when you set up tools and you pick tools and you implement them, you should be thinking, what's going to happen a year from now if I don't change anything?

vocabulary.definition: A method or way of doing something, particularly in problem-solving or decision-making contexts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, an approach can refer to a strategic methodology employed to achieve objectives or tackle challenges, such as a customer-centric approach or a data-driven approach.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a personal or unique perspective, suggesting that different individuals or organizations may have varied methods for addressing similar issues.

text: I think the most superhuman user acquisition people out there are engineers and they don't need a marketing technologist because they set up the tool themself. They know how the paid campaign runs and they just do it all.
speaker: Austin Hay
context: Lenny asks about the relationship between MarTech people and paid growth specialists. Austin explains that the most effective user acquisition professionals are those with engineering backgrounds who can handle both the technical setup and campaign management themselves. However, he notes this is rare and typically occurs at small startups where engineers are forced to learn marketing out of necessity when founders tell them to "figure out" advertising platforms.
text_ko: 제 생각엔 유저 획득(user acquisition) 분야에서 정말 뛰어난 사람들은 엔지니어들이에요. 이분들은 툴을 스스로 세팅해서 마케팅 테크놀로지스트(marketing technologist)가 따로 필요 없어요. 유료 캠페인(paid campaign)이 어떻게 돌아가는지 잘 알고, 그냥 다 직접 해요.
text_zh: 我觉得最厉害的用户获取(user acquisition)人才其实是工程师，他们根本不需要什么营销技术专家，因为工具都是自己搭建的。付费推广(paid campaign)怎么跑他们门儿清，全都自己搞定。
text_es: Creo que los mejores en captación de usuarios (user acquisition) son los ingenieros, y no necesitan a alguien de marketing tecnológico porque ellos mismos configuran las herramientas. Saben perfectamente cómo funcionan las campañas pagadas y se encargan de todo.
key_sentence: Superhuman user acquisition people are engineers who set up tools themselves.
original_text: I think the most superhuman user acquisition people out there are engineers and they don't need a marketing technologist because they set up the tool themself. They know how the paid campaign runs and they just do it all. And you'll typically find these super humans at small startups where the engineer is just told by the co-founder, hey, go figure out how Facebook ads work.

vocabulary.definition: User acquisition refers to the process of gaining new users or customers for a product or service, often through various marketing strategies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech settings, user acquisition is critical for growth, as it directly impacts a company's customer base and revenue potential.
vocabulary.nuance: While user acquisition focuses on attracting new users, it is important to balance this with user retention strategies to ensure long-term success.

vocabulary.definition: A marketing technologist is a professional who combines marketing expertise with technical skills to implement and optimize marketing technologies and strategies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, marketing technologists play a crucial role in leveraging data and tools to enhance marketing effectiveness and drive user engagement.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a blend of creativity and analytical skills, making it distinct from traditional marketing roles that may not require technical proficiency.

vocabulary.definition: A paid campaign is a marketing strategy that involves paying for advertisements to promote a product or service across various platforms.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, paid campaigns are commonly used to quickly reach target audiences, generate leads, and drive conversions, often complementing organic marketing efforts.
vocabulary.nuance: Paid campaigns can vary in scale and duration, and their effectiveness often depends on careful targeting and budget management.
